megahit_fix_cpu_1.description: Fix number of CPUs for MEGAHIT to 1. Not increased with retries.
megahit_fix_cpu_1.help_text:
MEGAHIT only generates reproducible results when run single-threaded. 

When using this parameter do not change the number of CPUs for the `megahit` process with a custom config file. This would result in an error.

Default: The number of CPUs is specified in the `base.config` file, and increased with each retry.

spades_fix_cpus.description: Fix number of CPUs used by SPAdes. Not increased with retries.
spades_fix_cpus.help_text:
SPAdes is designed to be deterministic for a given number of threads. To generate reproducible results fix the number of CPUs using this parameter.

When using this parameter do not change the number of CPUs for the `spades` process with a custom config file. This would result in an error.

Default: -1 (the number of CPUs is specified in the `base.config` or in a custom config file, and increased with each retry).

spadeshybrid_fix_cpus.description: Fix number of CPUs used by SPAdes hybrid. Not increased with retries.
spadeshybrid_fix_cpus.help_text:
SPAdes is designed to be deterministic for a given number of threads. To generate reproducible results fix the number of CPUs using this parameter.

When using this parameter do not change the number of CPUs for the `spadeshybrid` process with a custom config file. This would result in an error.

Default: -1 (the number of CPUs is specified in the `base.config` or in a custom config file, and increased with each retry).

metabat_rng_seed.help_text: MetaBAT2 is run by default with a fixed seed within this pipeline, thus producing reproducible results. You can set it also to any other positive integer to ensure reproducibility. Set the parameter to 0 to use a random seed.

clip_tool.description: Specify which adapter clipping tool to use.

save_clipped_reads.description: Specify to save the resulting clipped FASTQ files to --outdir.

reads_minlength.description: The minimum length of reads must have to be retained for downstream analysis.

fastp_qualified_quality.description: Minimum phred quality value of a base to be qualified in fastp.
fastp_qualified_quality.help: Reads with more than 40% of unqualified bases will be discarded.

fastp_cut_mean_quality.description: The mean quality requirement used for per read sliding window cutting by fastp.
fastp_cut_mean_quality.help: Used in combination with the fastp options '--cut_front' and '--cut_tail'. If the mean quality within a window (of size 4) is below `--fastp_cut_mean_quality`, the bases are dropped and the sliding window is moved further, otherwise it stops.

fastp_save_trimmed_fail.description: Save reads that fail fastp filtering in a separate file. Not used downstream.

fastp_trim_polyg.description: Turn on detecting and trimming of poly-G tails
fastp_trim_polyg.help_text:
This is particularly useful when dealing with Illumina 2 colour chemistry sequencing platforms, that will record 'G' in the absence of any light emitted.

See [here](https://sequencing.qcfail.com/articles/illumina-2-colour-chemistry-can-overcall-high-confidence-g-bases/) for more information on the artefact.

adapterremoval_minquality.description: The minimum base quality for low-quality base trimming by AdapterRemoval.

adapterremoval_trim_quality_stretch.description: Turn on quality trimming by consecutive stretch of low quality bases, rather than by window.
adapterremoval_trim_quality_stretch.help_text:
Default base-quality trimming is set to trim by 'windows', as in FastP. Specifying this flag will use trim via contiguous stretch of low quality bases (Ns) instead.

> Replaces --trimwindows 4 with --trimqualities in AdapterRemoval

adapterremoval_adapter1.description: Forward read adapter to be trimmed by AdapterRemoval.

adapterremoval_adapter2.description: Reverse read adapter to be trimmed by AdapterRemoval for paired end data.

host_genome.help_text:
This parameter is mutually exclusive with `--host_fasta`. Host read removal is done with Bowtie2. 
Both the iGenomes FASTA file as well as corresponding, already pre-built Bowtie 2 index files will be used.
host_genome.description: Name of iGenomes reference for host contamination removal.

host_fasta.description: Fasta reference file for host contamination removal.
host_fasta.help_text: This parameter is mutually exclusive with `--host_genome`. The reference can be masked. Host read removal is done with Bowtie2.

host_fasta_bowtie2index.description: Bowtie2 index directory corresponding to `--host_fasta` reference file for host contamination removal.
host_fasta_bowtie2index.help_text: This parameter must be used in combination with `--host_fasta`, and should be a directory containing files from the output of `bowtie2-build`, i.e. files ending in `.bt2`

host_removal_verysensitive.description: Use the `--very-sensitive` instead of the`--sensitive`setting for Bowtie 2 to map reads against the host genome.

host_removal_save_ids.description: Save the read IDs of removed host reads.

save_hostremoved_reads.description: Specify to save input FASTQ files with host reads removed to --outdir.

keep_phix.description: Keep reads similar to the Illumina internal standard PhiX genome.

phix_reference.description: Genome reference used to remove Illumina PhiX contaminant reads.
phix_reference.help_text: If not supplied, and keeping phix is turned off, an included genome (GCA_002596845.1) will be used

skip_clipping.description: Skip read preprocessing using fastp or adapterremoval.

skip_shortread_qc.description: Skip all default QC steps for short reads (adapter trimming, phiX removal).
skip_shortread_qc.help: Skips clipping and removal of phiX sequences. Does not affect host sequence removal as this is opt in. Does not prevent FastQC from running if host removal is enabled.

skip_fastqc.description: Skip running FastQC on short reads both before and after QC.
skip_fastqc.help: Skips running FastQC on short reads. Most metrics are redundant with reports from adapter clipping tools, but some metrics are not available from adapter clipping tools. This option is useful to save time and resources when running the pipeline.

save_phixremoved_reads.description: Specify to save input FASTQ files with phiX reads removed to --outdir.

bbnorm.description: Run BBnorm to normalize sequence depth.

bbnorm_target.description: Set BBnorm target maximum depth to this number.

bbnorm_min.description: Set BBnorm minimum depth to this number.

save_bbnorm_reads.description: Save normalized read files to output directory.

skip_adapter_trimming.description: Skip removing adapter sequences from long reads.

skip_longread_qc.description: Skip all default QC steps for long reads (adapter trimming, filtering, removal of lambda sequences).
skip_longread_qc.help: Skips adapter trimming and filtering, but not host sequence removal.

longreads_min_length.description: Discard any read which is shorter than this value.

longreads_min_quality.description: Discard any read which has a mean quality score lower than this value.

longreads_keep_percent.description: Keep this percent of bases. Only used by filtlong.

longreads_length_weight.description: The higher the more important is read length when choosing the best reads. Only used by filtlong.
longreads_length_weight.help_text:
The default value focuses on length instead of quality to improve assembly size.
In order to assign equal weights to read lengths and read qualities set this parameter to 1.
This might be useful, for example, to benefit indirectly from the removal of short host reads (causing lower qualities for reads not overlapping filtered short reads).

keep_lambda.description: Keep reads similar to the ONT internal standard Escherichia virus Lambda genome.

lambda_reference.description: Genome reference used to remove ONT Lambda contaminant reads.
lambda_reference.help_text: If not supplied, and keeping lambda is turned off, an included genome (GCA_000840245.1) will be used

save_lambdaremoved_reads.description: Specify to save input FASTQ files with lamba reads removed  to --outdir.

save_porechop_reads.description: Specify to save the resulting clipped FASTQ files to --outdir.

save_filtered_longreads.description: Specify to save the resulting length filtered long read FASTQ files to --outdir.

longread_adaptertrimming_tool.description: Specify which long read adapter trimming tool to use.

longread_filtering_tool.description: Specify which long read filtering tool to use.

filtlong_filtering_by_shortreads.description: Filter long reads against short reads when using filtlong.
filtlong_filtering_by_shortreads.help_text: Only applies when `--longread_filtering_tool filtlong` and short reads are supplied. When enabled, filtlong derives long read quality from k-mer matches to the short reads instead of the Phred scores. This can discard long reads not overlapping the short reads, leading to data loss if short read coverage is poor or the metagenomes differ.

cat_db.description: Database for taxonomic classification of metagenome assembled genomes. Can be either a zipped file or a directory containing the extracted output of such.
cat_db.help_text: E.g. https://tbb.bio.uu.nl/bastiaan/CAT_prepare/CAT_prepare_20210107.tar.gz. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `--cat_db_generate`. The file needs to contain a folder named `*taxonomy*` and `*database*` that hold the respective files.

cat_db_generate.help_text: Download the taxonomy files from NCBI taxonomy, the nr database and generate CAT database. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `--cat_db`. Useful to build a CAT database with the same DIAMOND version as used for running CAT classification, avoiding compatibility problems.

save_cat_db.description: Save the CAT database generated when specified by `--cat_db_generate`.
save_cat_db.help_text: Useful to allow reproducibility, as old versions of prebuild CAT databases do not always remain accessible and underlying NCBI taxonomy and nr databases change.

cat_allow_unofficial_lineages.description: Allow unofficial lineages in CAT classification.
cat_allow_unofficial_lineages.help_text:
By default, CAT only provides classifications enumerated at standard Linnaean taxonomic ranks. This option enables the output of non-standard ranks, which is useful with custom databases.

Note that it disables classification result summarization, as this is not supported by CAT_pack summarise.

cat_classify_unbinned.description: Classify unbinned contigs with CAT (contig mode).
cat_classify_unbinned.help_text: By default, nf-core/mag only runs CAT taxonomic classification on bins. Specifying this parameter will  additionally run CAT classification on all unbinned contigs, which can be useful to get an idea of the taxonomic composition of the unbinned contigs. In some cases this may significantly extend run time of the pipeline.

cat_no_suggestive_asterisks.description: Specify to turn off CAT marking in output files most probable hits (when multiple) with an asterix.

skip_gtdbtk.description: Skip the running of GTDB, as well as the automatic download of the database

gtdb_db.description: Specify the location of a GTDBTK database. Can be either an uncompressed directory or a `.tar.gz` archive. If not specified will be downloaded for you when GTDBTK or binning QC is not skipped.

gtdbtk_min_completeness.description: Min. bin completeness (in %) required to apply GTDB-tk classification.
gtdbtk_min_completeness.help_text: Completeness assessed with any of the bin QC tools (BUSCO, CheckM, CheckM2). A bin passes if at least one QC tool reports completeness at or above the threshold. Must be greater than 0 (min. 0.01) to avoid GTDB-tk errors. If too low, GTDB-tk classification results can be impaired due to not enough marker genes!

gtdbtk_max_contamination.description: Max. bin contamination (in %) allowed to apply GTDB-tk classification.
gtdbtk_max_contamination.help_text: Contamination assessed with any of the bin QC tools (BUSCO, CheckM, CheckM2). A bin passes if at least one QC tool reports contamination at or below the threshold. If too high, GTDB-tk classification results can be impaired due to contamination!

gtdbtk_min_perc_aa.description: Min. fraction of AA (in %) in the MSA for bins to be kept.

gtdbtk_min_af.description: Min. alignment fraction to consider closest genome.

gtdbtk_pplacer_cpus.description: Number of CPUs used for the by GTDB-Tk run tool pplacer.
gtdbtk_pplacer_cpus.help_text: A low number of CPUs helps to reduce the memory required/reported by GTDB-Tk. See also the [GTDB-Tk documentation](https://ecogenomics.github.io/GTDBTk/faq.html#gtdb-tk-reaches-the-memory-limit-pplacer-crashes).

gtdbtk_pplacer_useram.description: Speed up pplacer step of GTDB-Tk by loading to memory.
gtdbtk_pplacer_useram.help_text: Will be faster than writing to disk (default setting), however at the expense of much larger memory (RAM) requirements for GTDBTK/CLASSIFY.

gtdbtk_use_full_tree.description: Specify to have GTDBTk to use the full bacterial tree rather than the split tree (requires more memory!)

gtdbtk_place_species.description: Specify to disable fast classification of genomes by ANI using skani in GTDB-Tk.

gtdbtk_skip_aniscreen.description: [DEPRECATED] Use `--gtdbtk_place_species` instead. Specify to disable fast classification of genomes by ANI using skani in GTDB-Tk.

gtdbtk_single_job.description: Run GTDB-Tk classification for all bins in a single job, rather than one job per sample/assembler/binner group.
gtdbtk_single_job.help_text: By default nf-core/mag submits a separate GTDBTK_CLASSIFYWF job per group of bins. When classifying very large numbers of bins, it can be more efficient to run all bins together in one job, as steps such as skani and pplacer are then performed once over the whole dataset instead of being repeated per job.

coassemble_group.description: Co-assemble samples within one group, instead of assembling each sample separately.

spades_options.description: Additional custom options for SPAdes and SPAdesHybrid. Do not specify `--meta` as this will be added for you!
spades_options.help_text: An example is adjusting k-mers ("-k 21,33,55,77") or adding [advanced options](https://github.com/ablab/spades#advanced-options). But not --meta, -t, -m, -o or --out-prefix, because these are already in use. Must be used like this: --spades_options='-k 21,33,55,77'

spades_downstreaminput.description: Specify whether to use contigs or scaffolds assembled by SPAdes
spades_downstreaminput.help_text: By default the SPAdes documentation recommends using scaffolds rather than contigs, as these are longer as they combine multiple contigs. However there is an increased risk of misassemblies or chimeras. Use this flag to specify to just use contigs for downstream processes such as binning.

megahit_options.help_text: An example is adjusting presets (e.g. "--presets meta-large"), k-mers (e.g. "-k 21,33,55,77") or adding other [advanced options](https://github.com/voutcn/megahit#advanced-usage). For example, increase the minimum k-mer in the event of an error message such as "Too many vertices in the unitig graph, you may increase the kmer size to remove tons of erroneous kmers." in the MEGAHIT log file. But not --threads, --memory, -o or input read files, because these are already in use. Must be used like this: --megahit_options='--presets meta-large'

ale_per_base_output.description: Enable ALE per-base output. This output can be very large (tens of GB).

run_pypolca.description: Run PyPOLCA polishing on long-read assemblies before binning.

prokka_with_compliance.help_text:
Sometimes Prokka will complain that your contig names are too long and fail.

This particularly happens with metaSPAdes assemblies.

You can turn on this flag which will tell Prokka to truncate the contig names for you.
However this also requires you to specify a sequencing centre name (specified with `--prokka_compliance_centre`).

:::warning
Truncating contig names may make it harder to associated contig annotations with their original contigs!
:::
prokka_with_compliance.description: Turn on Prokka complicance mode for truncating contig names for NCBI/ENA compatibility.

prokka_compliance_centre.help_text: Specify the sequencing centre name for making NCBI Genbank/ENA compatible annotation files (required when specifying `--prokka_with_compliance`).
prokka_compliance_centre.description: Specify sequencing centre name required for Prokka's compliance mode.

prokka_fast_mode.description: Specify to skip CDS/product searching in Prokka runs

skip_metaeuk.description: [DEPRECATED] This parameter no longer has any effect and will be removed in a future release. MetaEuk only runs when `--metaeuk_db` or `--metaeuk_mmseqs_db` is supplied.

metaeuk_mmseqs_db.description: A string containing the name of one of the databases listed in the [mmseqs2 documentation](https://github.com/soedinglab/MMseqs2/wiki#downloading-databases). This database will be downloaded and formatted for eukaryotic genome annotation. Incompatible with --metaeuk_db.
metaeuk_mmseqs_db.help_text: mmseqs2 lists a large number of databases, not all of which are appropriate for use with MetaEuk. MetaEuk requires protein inputs, so you should select one of the Aminoacid or Profile options.

metaeuk_db.description: Path to either a local fasta file of protein sequences, or to a directory containing an MMseqs2-formatted database, for annotation of eukaryotic genomes.
metaeuk_db.help_text:
One option would be the databases from the MetaEuk publication (https://wwwuser.gwdg.de/~compbiol/metaeuk/), however it should be noted that these are focused on marine eukaryotes.

If supplying an mmseqs database, you must supply a directory that _within_ it has the `database`, `database.dbtype`, `database_h` etc. files. For example, for a pre-downloaded Kalamari database, you would supply `--mmseqs_db /<path>/<to>/mmseqs_db/Kalamari/. Where if you were to look inside the database you would see `mmseqs_db/Kalamari/database_h`

save_mmseqs_db.description: Save the downloaded mmseqs2 database specified in `--metaeuk_mmseqs_db`.

genomad_db.description: Database for virus classification with geNomad
genomad_db.help_text: Must be a directory containing the uncompressed contents from https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.6994741 (nf-core/mag tested with v1.1)

genomad_min_score.description: Minimum geNomad score for a sequence to be considered viral

genomad_splits.description: Number of groups that geNomad's MMSeqs2 databse should be split into (reduced memory requirements)

binning_map_mode.description: Defines mapping strategy to compute co-abundances for binning, i.e. which samples will be mapped against the assembly.
binning_map_mode.help_text:
Available: `all`, `group` or `own`. Note that `own` cannot be specified in combination with `--coassemble_group`.

Note that specifying `all` without additionally specifying `--coassemble_group` results in `n^2` mapping processes for each assembly method, where `n` is the number of samples.

bin_metabinner_scale.help_text: Dataset scale; eg. small,large,huge (default:large); Users can choose `huge` to run MetaBinner on huge datasets with lower memory requirements.

semibin_rng_seed.help_text: SemiBin2 is run by default with a fixed seed within this pipeline, thus producing reproducible results. You can set it also to any other positive integer to ensure reproducibility. Set the parameter to 0 to use a random seed.

semibin_environment.description: Pre-trained model for SemiBin2 for single sample assemblies
semibin_environment.help_text: SemiBin2 can use a pre-trained model when working with an assembly of a single sample (i.e. without `--coassemble_group` and with `--binning_map_mode own`). The model will be ignored when several samples are used for one assembly. Choose a model that fits your environment best. Default is `global`, a generic model.

min_contig_size.description: Minimum contig size to be considered for binning and for bin quality check.
min_contig_size.help_text: For forwarding into downstream analysis, i.e. QUAST and BUSCO, and reporting.

min_length_unbinned_contigs.description: Minimal length of contigs that are not part of any bin but treated as individual genome.
min_length_unbinned_contigs.help_text: Contigs that do not fulfill the thresholds of `--min_length_unbinned_contigs` and `--max_unbinned_contigs` are pooled for downstream analysis and reporting, except contigs that also do not fulfill `--min_contig_size` are not considered further.

max_unbinned_contigs.description: Maximal number of contigs that are not part of any bin but treated as individual genome.
max_unbinned_contigs.help_text: Contigs that do not fulfill the thresholds of `--min_length_unbinned_contigs` and `--max_unbinned_contigs` are pooled for downstream analysis and reporting, except contigs that also do not fulfill `--min_contig_size` are not considered further.

bin_min_size.description: Specify the shortest length a bin should be to retain for downstream processing (in base pairs)
bin_min_size.help_text: This can speed up downstream processing by removing 'nonsense' bins (e.g. badly binned single short-contig bins, or unnaturally large bins). By default there is no lower limit the size of bins allowed to pass.

bin_max_size.description: Specify the longest length a bin should be to retain for downstream processing (in base pairs). By default no limit.
bin_max_size.help_text: This can speed up downstream processing by removing 'nonsense' bins (e.g. badly binned single short-contig bins, or unnaturally large bins). By default there is no upper limit on size of bins allowed to pass.

bin_seqkit_stats_max_forks.description: Limit the number of concurrent SEQKIT_STATS jobs used for bin size calculation.
bin_seqkit_stats_max_forks.help_text: Bins from each binner are sent to SEQKIT_STATS as soon as that binner finishes, which can spawn many short jobs (roughly samples * assemblers * binners). On schedulers that dislike large numbers of tiny jobs, set this to cap how many run at once.

bin_concoct_chunksize.description: Specify length of sub-contigs cut up prior CONCOCT binning

bin_concoct_overlap.description: Specify the overlap between each sub-contig prior CONCOCT binning

bin_concoct_donotconcatlast.description: Specify to not append the last contig less than sub-contig length to the last correct length contig

bowtie2_mode.description: Specify alternative Bowtie2 settings for aligning reads back against the assembly.
bowtie2_mode.help_text: You can specify here Bowtie2 alignment options. For example: `--very-fast` , `--very-sensitive-local -N 1` , ... Must be used like this: --bowtie2_mode="--very-sensitive". By default no settings are defined, thus Bowtie2 runs with it's own internal defaults (e.g. end-to-end alignment)

save_assembly_mapped_reads.description: Save the output of mapping raw reads back to assembled contigs
save_assembly_mapped_reads.help_text: Specify to save the BAM and BAI files generated when mapping input reads back to the assembled contigs (performed in preparation for binning and contig depth estimations).

bin_domain_classification.description: Enable domain-level (prokaryote or eukaryote) classification of bins using Tiara. Processes which are domain-specific will then only receive bins matching the domain requirement.
bin_domain_classification.help_text: Enable this if it is likely that your metagenome samples contain a mixture of eukaryotic and prokaryotic genomes. This will ensure that prokaryote-only steps only receive putatively prokaryotic genomes, and vice-versa. Additionally, may improve the performance of DAS Tool by ensuring it only receives prokaryotic genomes.

bin_domain_classification_tool.description: Specify which tool to use for domain classification of bins. Currently only 'tiara' is implemented.

tiara_min_length.description: Minimum contig length for Tiara to use for domain classification. For accurate classification, should be longer than 3000 bp.

exclude_unbins_from_postbinning.description: Exclude unbinned contigs in the post-binning steps (bin QC, taxonomic classification, and annotation steps).
exclude_unbins_from_postbinning.help_text: If you're not interested in assemby results that are not considered 'genome level', excluding unbinned contigs can greatly speed up downstream steps such as Prokka, that can be quite slow and spin up many tasks.

longread_percentidentity.description: Specify a minimum percent identity filter for long reads mapping back to assembled contigs.
longread_percentidentity.help_text: If specified, this parameter sets the `--percentIdentity` flag of the `metabat2 jgisummarizebamcontigdepths` command that is used to generate a read-depth per contig depth post assembly mapping. It can be useful in some cases to get more accurate depth coverages for binning by removing spurious alignments that can inflate coverage.

shortread_percentidentity.description: Specify a minimum percent identity filter for short reads mapping back to assembled contigs.
shortread_percentidentity.help_text: If specified, this parameter sets the `--percentIdentity` flag of the `metabat2 jgisummarizebamcontigdepths` command that is used to generate a read-depth per contig depth post assembly mapping. It can be useful in some cases to get more accurate depth coverages for binning by removing spurious alignments that can inflate coverage.

skip_binqc.description: Disable bin QC with BUSCO, CheckM or CheckM2.

run_busco.description: Enable running BUSCO during bin QC.

run_checkm.description: Enable running CheckM during bin QC.

run_checkm2.description: Enable running CheckM2 during bin QC.

busco_db.description: Download URL, local tar.gz archive, or local uncompressed directory for an *_odb10 or *_odb12 BUSCO lineage dataset.
busco_db.help_text:
E.g. https://busco-data.ezlab.org/v5/data/lineages/bacteria_odb10.2024-01-08.tar.gz, `/path/to/bacteria_odb10.2024-01-08.tar.gz`.

For more details, check the [BUSCO section in the usage documentation](https://nf-co.re/mag/latest/docs/usage/#busco).

busco_db_lineage.description: Name of the BUSCO *_odb10 or *_odb12 lineage to check against. Additionally supports 'auto', 'auto_prok' and 'auto_euk' for automatic lineage selection mode.
busco_db_lineage.help_text:
Typically used in combination with `--busco_db`, corresponding to the lineage files supplied within the `--busco_db` file or directory.

If supplying without a `--busco_db`, will require an internet connection to work!

save_busco_db.description: Save the used BUSCO lineage datasets provided via `--busco_db`.
save_busco_db.help_text: Useful to allow reproducibility, as BUSCO datasets are frequently updated and old versions do not always remain accessible.

busco_clean.description: Enable clean-up of temporary files created during BUSCO runs.
busco_clean.help_text: By default, BUSCO creates a large number of intermediate files every run. This may cause problems on some clusters which have file number limits in plate, particularly with large numbers of bins. Enabling this option cleans these files, reducing the total file count of the work directory.

checkm_download_url.description: URL pointing to checkM database for auto download, if local path not supplied.
checkm_download_url.help_text: You can use this parameter to point to an online copy of the checkM database TAR archive that the pipeline will use for auto download if a local path is not supplied to `--checkm_db`.

checkm_db.description: Path to local folder containing already downloaded and uncompressed CheckM database.
checkm_db.help_text: The pipeline can also download this for you if not specified, and you can save the resulting directory into your output directory by specifying `--save_checkm_data`. You should move this directory to somewhere else on your machine (and supply back to the pipeline in future runs again with `--checkm_db`.

save_checkm_data.description: Save the used CheckM reference files downloaded when not using --checkm_db parameter.
save_checkm_data.help_text: If specified, the directories and files decompressed from the `tar.gz` file downloaded from the [CheckM FTP server](https://data.ace.uq.edu.au/public/CheckM_databases/) will be stored in your output directory alongside your CheckM results.

checkm2_db.description: Path to local file of an already downloaded and uncompressed CheckM2 database file (.dmnd file).
checkm2_db.help_text: The pipeline can also download this for you if not specified, and you can save the resulting directory into your output directory by specifying `--save_checkm2_data`. You should move this file to somewhere else on your machine (and supply back to the pipeline in future runs again with `--checkm2_db`).

checkm2_db_version.description: CheckM2 database version number to download (Zenodo record ID, for reference check the canonical reference https://zenodo.org/records/5571251, and pick the Zenodo ID of the database version of your choice).

save_checkm2_data.description: Save the used CheckM2 reference files downloaded when not using --checkm2_db parameter.
save_checkm2_data.help_text: If specified, the directories and files decompressed from the `tar.gz` file downloaded from the [Zenodo repository](https://zenodo.org/records/5571251) will be stored in your output directory alongside your CheckM2 results.

refine_bins_dastool.description: Turn on bin refinement using DAS Tool.

refine_bins_dastool_threshold.description: Specify single-copy gene score threshold for bin refinement.
refine_bins_dastool_threshold.help_text:
Score threshold for single-copy gene selection algorithm to keep selecting bins, with a value ranging from 0-1.

For description of scoring algorithm, see: Sieber, Christian M. K., et al. 2018. Nature Microbiology 3 (7): 836–43. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-018-0171-1.

> Modifies DAS Tool parameter --score_threshold

refine_bins_dastool_savecontig2bin.description: Specify to save contig to bin maps used for bin refinement

postbinning_input.description: Specify which binning output is sent for downstream annotation, taxonomic classification, bin quality control etc.
postbinning_input.help_text:
`raw_bins_only`: only bins (and unbinned contigs) from the binners.
`refined_bins_only`: only bins (and unbinned contigs) from the bin refinement step.
`both`: bins and unbinned contigs from both the binning and bin refinement steps.

run_gunc.description: Turn on GUNC genome chimerism checks

gunc_db.description: Specify a path to a pre-downloaded GUNC dmnd database file

gunc_database_type.description: Specify which database to auto-download if not supplying own

gunc_save_db.description: Save the used GUNC reference files downloaded when not using --gunc_db parameter.
gunc_save_db.help_text: If specified, the corresponding DIAMOND file downloaded from the GUNC server will be stored in your output directory alongside your GUNC results.

generate_bigmag_file.description: Make a BIgMAG input file including GUNC results.
generate_bigmag_file.help_text: It requires --run_gunc and --run_checkm2 to be executed. BINQC, GTDB-TK, QUAST nor BUSCO can't be skipped.

ancient_dna.description: Turn on/off the ancient DNA subworkflow

skip_ancient_damagecorrection.description: deactivate damage correction of ancient contigs using variant and consensus calling

freebayes_min_basequality.description: minimum base quality required for variant calling

freebayes_minallelefreq.description: minimum minor allele frequency for considering variants

bcftools_view_high_variant_quality.description: minimum genotype quality for considering a variant high quality

bcftools_view_medium_variant_quality.description: minimum genotype quality for considering a variant medium quality

bcftools_view_minimal_allelesupport.description: minimum number of bases supporting the alternative allele

substeps: MAG 质量、分类与功能注释

nodes.name: 整理丰度表与样本信息
nodes.description: 整理丰度表与样本信息，结果独立保存，可在对话中调整输入和参数。

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a samplesheet with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 5 columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/atacseq/docs/usage#introduction).

fragment_size.description: Estimated fragment size used to extend single-end reads.

seq_center.description: Sequencing center information to be added to read group of BAM files.

read_length.description: Read length used to calculate or retrieve pre-computed MACS2 genome size for peak calling if `--macs_gsize` isn't provided.
read_length.help_text: Read length together with the genome fasta are used to calculate MACS2 genome size using the `khmer` program as explained [here](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/feature/effectiveGenomeSize.html#effective-genome-size). For all the genomes present in the `igenomes.config` the genome size has been already precomputed and the read length is then used to retrieve the corresponding value

with_control.help_text: Use this to indicate that your samplesheet lists controls.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

genome.help_text:
If using a reference genome configured in the pipeline using iGenomes, use this parameter to give the ID for the reference. This is then used to build the full paths for all required reference genome files e.g. `--genome GRCh38`. 

See the [nf-core website docs](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for more details.

fasta.help_text: This parameter is *mandatory* if `--genome` is not specified. If you don't have the appropriate alignment index available this will be generated for you automatically. Combine with `--save_reference` to save alignment index for future runs.

gtf.help_text: This parameter is *mandatory* if `--genome` is not specified.

gff.help_text: This parameter must be specified if `--genome` or `--gtf` are not specified.

bwa_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built BWA index.

bowtie2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Bowtie2 index.

chromap_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Chromap index.

star_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built STAR index.

gene_bed.description: Path to BED file containing gene intervals. This will be created from the GTF file if not specified.

tss_bed.description: Path to BED file containing transcription start sites. This will be created from the gene BED file if not specified.

macs_gsize.description: Effective genome size parameter required by MACS2.
macs_gsize.help_text: [Effective genome size](https://github.com/taoliu/MACS#-g--gsize) parameter required by MACS2. If using an iGenomes reference these have been provided when `--genome` is set as *GRCh37*, *GRCh38*, *GRCm38*, *WBcel235*, *BDGP6*, *R64-1-1*, *EF2*, *hg38*, *hg19* and *mm10*. For other genomes, if this parameter is not specified then the MACS2 peak-calling and differential analysis will be skipped.

blacklist.description: Path to blacklist regions in BED format, used for filtering alignments.
blacklist.help_text: If provided, alignments that overlap with the regions in this file will be filtered out (see [ENCODE blacklists](https://sites.google.com/site/anshulkundaje/projects/blacklists)). The file should be in BED format. Blacklisted regions for *GRCh37*, *GRCh38*, *GRCm38*, *hg19*, *hg38*, *mm10* are bundled with the pipeline in the [`blacklists`](../assets/blacklists/) directory, and as such will be automatically used if any of those genomes are specified with the `--genome` parameter.

mito_name.description: Name of Mitochondrial chomosome in reference assembly e.g. chrM.
mito_name.help_text: Reads aligning to this contig are filtered out if a valid identifier is provided otherwise this step is skipped. Where possible these have been provided in the [`igenomes.config`](../conf/igenomes.config).

save_reference.description: If generated by the pipeline save the aligner index (e.g. BWA) in the results directory.
save_reference.help_text: If the index generated by the aligner is generated by the pipeline use this parameter to save it to your results folder. These can then be used for future pipeline runs, reducing processing times.

igenomes_base.description: Directory / URL base for iGenomes references.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

keep_mito.description: Reads mapping to mitochondrial contig are not filtered from alignments.

ataqv_mito_reference.description: Sets the value of the ataqv --mitochondrial-reference-name argument
ataqv_mito_reference.help_text: By default takes the value of the mito_name parameter, if set. However, some plants and algae have chloroplast genomes in addition to a mitochondrial genome and thus mito_name can have values as multiple names that are separated by a | symbol that will break ataqv, in these cases this parameter can be used to overwrite these values.

clip_r1.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 5' end of read 1 (or single-end reads).

clip_r2.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 5' end of read 2 (paired-end reads only).

three_prime_clip_r1.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 3' end of read 1 AFTER adapter/quality trimming has been performed.

three_prime_clip_r2.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 3' end of read 2 AFTER adapter/quality trimming has been performed.

trim_nextseq.description: Instructs Trim Galore to apply the --nextseq=X option, to trim based on quality after removing poly-G tails.
trim_nextseq.help_text: This enables the option Cutadapt `--nextseq-trim=3'CUTOFF` option via Trim Galore, which will set a quality cutoff (that is normally given with -q instead), but qualities of G bases are ignored. This trimming is in common for the NextSeq- and NovaSeq-platforms, where basecalls without any signal are called as high-quality G bases.

min_trimmed_reads.description: 会影响比对、过滤或区域判定；按实验类型调整，通常保留原流程默认。
min_trimmed_reads.label: 过滤后最低读段数

skip_trimming.help_text: Use this if your input FastQ files have already been trimmed outside of the workflow or if you're very confident that there is no adapter contamination in your data.

save_trimmed.description: Save the trimmed FastQ files in the results directory.
save_trimmed.help_text: By default, trimmed FastQ files will not be saved to the results directory. Specify this flag (or set to true in your config file) to copy these files to the results directory when complete.

aligner.description: 会影响比对、过滤或区域判定；按实验类型调整，通常保留原流程默认。
aligner.label: 比对软件

keep_dups.description: Duplicate reads are not filtered from alignments.

keep_multi_map.description: Reads mapping to multiple locations are not filtered from alignments.

bwa_min_score.description: Don’t output BWA MEM alignments with score lower than this parameter.

skip_merge_replicates.description: Do not perform alignment merging and downstream analysis by merging replicates i.e. only do this by merging resequenced libraries.
skip_merge_replicates.help_text: An additional series of steps are performed by the pipeline for merging the replicates from the same experimental group. This is primarily to increase the sequencing depth in order to perform downstream analyses such as footprinting. Specifying this parameter means that these steps will not be performed.

save_align_intermeds.description: Save the intermediate BAM files from the alignment step.
save_align_intermeds.help_text: By default, intermediate BAM files will not be saved. The final BAM files created after the appropriate filtering step are always saved to limit storage usage. Set this parameter to also save other intermediate BAM files.

save_unaligned.description: Where possible, save unaligned reads from either STAR, HISAT2 or Salmon to the results directory.
save_unaligned.help_text: This may either be in the form of FastQ or BAM files depending on the options available for that particular tool.

bamtools_filter_pe_config.description: BAMTools JSON file with custom filters for paired-end data.

bamtools_filter_se_config.description: BAMTools JSON file with custom filters for single-end data.

narrow_peak.description: 会影响比对、过滤或区域判定；按实验类型调整，通常保留原流程默认。
narrow_peak.help_text: MACS2 is run by default with the [`--broad`](https://github.com/taoliu/MACS#--broad) flag. Specify this flag to call peaks in narrowPeak mode.
narrow_peak.label: 使用窄峰模式

broad_cutoff.description: 会影响比对、过滤或区域判定；按实验类型调整，通常保留原流程默认。
broad_cutoff.label: 宽峰显著性上限

macs_fdr.description: Minimum FDR (q-value) cutoff for peak detection, --macs_fdr and --macs_pvalue are mutually exclusive.

macs_pvalue.description: p-value cutoff for peak detection, --macs_fdr and --macs_pvalue are mutually exclusive. If --macs_pvalue cutoff is set, q-value will not be calculated and reported as -1 in the final .xls file.

min_reps_consensus.description: Number of biological replicates required from a given condition for a peak to contribute to a consensus peak.
min_reps_consensus.help_text: If you are confident you have good reproducibility amongst your replicates then you can increase the value of this parameter to create a 'reproducible' set of consensus peaks. For example, a value of 2 will mean peaks that have been called in at least 2 replicates will contribute to the consensus set of peaks, and as such peaks that are unique to a given replicate will be discarded.

save_macs_pileup.description: Instruct MACS2 to create bedGraph files normalised to signal per million reads.

skip_peak_qc.description: Skip MACS2 peak QC plot generation.

skip_peak_annotation.description: Skip annotation of MACS2 and consensus peaks with HOMER.

skip_consensus_peaks.description: Skip consensus peak generation, annotation and counting.

deseq2_vst.description: Use vst transformation instead of rlog with DESeq2.

skip_deseq2_qc.description: Skip DESeq2 PCA and heatmap plotting.

skip_qc.description: Skip all QC steps except for MultiQC.

max_cpus.description: Maximum number of CPUs that can be requested for any single job.
max_cpus.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the CPU requirement for each process. Should be an integer e.g. `--max_cpus 1`

max_memory.description: Maximum amount of memory that can be requested for any single job.
max_memory.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the memory requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_memory '8.GB'`

max_time.description: Maximum amount of time that can be requested for any single job.
max_time.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the time requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_time '2.h'`

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

fingerprint_bins.description: Number of genomic bins to use when calculating deepTools fingerprint plot.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

hook_url.description: Incoming hook URL for messaging service
hook_url.help_text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

validationShowHiddenParams.help_text: By default, parameters set as _hidden_ in the schema are not shown on the command line when a user runs with `--help`. Specifying this option will tell the pipeline to show all parameters.

validationFailUnrecognisedParams.description: Validation of parameters fails when an unrecognised parameter is found.
validationFailUnrecognisedParams.help_text: By default, when an unrecognised parameter is found, it returns a warinig.

validationLenientMode.description: Validation of parameters in lenient more.
validationLenientMode.help_text: Allows string values that are parseable as numbers or booleans. For further information see [JSONSchema docs](https://github.com/everit-org/json-schema#lenient-mode).

aligner.description: 会影响比对、过滤或区域判定；按实验类型调整，通常保留原流程默认。
aligner.help_text:
The nf-core/methylseq package is actually two pipelines in one. The default workflow uses [Bismark](http://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/bismark/) with [Bowtie2](http://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/bowtie2/index.shtml) as alignment tool: unless specified otherwise, nf-core/methylseq will run this pipeline.

Since bismark v0.21.0 it is also possible to use [HISAT2](https://ccb.jhu.edu/software/hisat2/index.shtml) as alignment tool. To run this workflow, invoke the pipeline with the command line flag `--aligner bismark_hisat`. HISAT2 also supports splice-aware alignment if analysis of RNA is desired (e.g. [SLAMseq](https://science.sciencemag.org/content/360/6390/800) experiments), a file containing a list of known splicesites can be provided with `--known_splices`.

The second workflow uses [BWA-Meth](https://github.com/brentp/bwa-meth) and [MethylDackel](https://github.com/dpryan79/methyldackel) instead of Bismark. To run this workflow, run the pipeline with the command line flag `--aligner bwameth`.

use_mem2.help_text: When using the BWA-Meth aligner (`--aligner bwameth`), this parameter enables the BWA-MEM2 algorithm which can provide improved performance and accuracy. The BWA-MEM2 algorithm is a drop-in replacement for BWA-MEM that is generally faster and more accurate. This option only applies when using BWA-Meth aligner.

pbat.help_text:
Specify this parameter when working with PBAT _(Post Bisulfite Adapter Tagging)_ libraries.

Using this parameter sets the `--pbat` flag when aligning with Bismark. This tells Bismark to align complementary strands (the opposite of `--directional`).

Additionally, this is a trimming preset equivalent to `--clip_r1 8` `--clip_r2 8` `--three_prime_clip_r1 8` `--three_prime_clip_r2 8`, unless `--skip_trimming_presets` is set to `true`

Use this parameter when working with RRBS _(Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing)_ data, that is digested using MspI.

Specifying `--rrbs` will pass on the `--rrbs` parameter to TrimGalore! See the [TrimGalore! documentation](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/blob/master/Docs/Trim_Galore_User_Guide.md#rrbs-specific-options-mspi-digested-material) to read more about the effects of this option.

This parameter also makes the pipeline skip the deduplication step.

non_directional.help_text:
By default, Bismark assumes that libraries are directional and does not align against complementary strands. If your library prep was not directional, use `--non_directional` to align against all four possible strands.

Note that the `--single_cell` and `--zymo` parameters both set the `--non_directional` workflow flag automatically.

cytosine_report.description: Output stranded cytosine report, following Bismark's bismark_methylation_extractor step.
cytosine_report.help_text: By default, Bismark does not produce stranded calls. With this option the output considers all Cs on both forward and reverse strands and reports their position, strand, trinucleotide context and methylation state.

relax_mismatches.description: Turn on to relax stringency for alignment (set allowed penalty with --num_mismatches).
relax_mismatches.help_text:
By default, Bismark is pretty strict about which alignments it accepts as valid. If you have good reason to believe that your reads will contain more mismatches than normal, this flags can be used to relax the stringency that Bismark uses when accepting alignments. This can greatly improve the number of aligned reads you get back, but may negatively impact the quality of your data.

Bismark uses the Bowtie alignment scoring mechanism to filter reads. Mismatches cost `-6`, gap opening `-5` and gap extension `-2`. So, a threshold of`-60` would allow 10 mismatches or ~ 8 x 1-2bp indels. The threshold is dependent on the length of reads, so a penalty value is used where `penalty * bp read length = threshold`.

The penalty value used by Bismark by default is `0.2`, so for 100bp reads this would be a threshold of `-20`. 

If you specifying the `--relax_mismatches` pipeline flag, Bismark instead uses `0.6`, or a threshold of `-60`. This adds the Bismark flag `--score_min L,0,-0.6` to the alignment command.

The penalty value can be modified using the `--num_mismatches` pipeline option.

num_mismatches.description: 0.6 will allow a penalty of bp * -0.6 - for 100bp reads (bismark default is 0.2)
num_mismatches.help_text:
Customise the penalty in the function used to filter reads based on mismatches. The parameter `--relax_mismatches` must also be specified.

See the parameter documentation for `--relax_mismatches` for an explanation.

no_overlap.description: Ignore read 2 methylation when it overlaps read 1
no_overlap.help_text: For paired-end reads it is theoretically possible that read_1 and read_2 overlap. To avoid scoring overlapping methylation calls twice, this is set to `true` by default. (Only methylation calls of read 1 are used since read 1 has historically higher quality basecalls than read 2). Whilst this option removes a bias towards more methylation calls in the center of sequenced fragments it may de facto remove a sizable proportion of the data. To count methylation data from both reads in overlapping regions, set this to `false`.

ignore_r1.description: Ignore methylation in first n bases of 5' end of R1
ignore_r1.help_text: Ignore the first <int> bp from the 5' end of Read 1 (or single-end alignment files) when processing the methylation call string. This can remove e.g. a restriction enzyme site at the start of each read or any other source of bias (such as PBAT-Seq data).

ignore_r2.description: Ignore methylation in first n bases of 5' end of R2
ignore_r2.help_text: Ignore the first <int> bp from the 5' end of Read 2 of paired-end sequencing results only. Since the first couple of bases in Read 2 of BS-Seq experiments show a severe bias towards non-methylation as a result of end-repairing sonicated fragments with unmethylated cytosines (see M-bias plot), it is recommended that the first couple of bp of Read 2 are removed before starting downstream analysis. Please see the section on M-bias plots in the Bismark User Guide for more details.

ignore_3prime_r1.description: Ignore methylation in last n bases of 3' end of R1
ignore_3prime_r1.help_text: Ignore the first <int> bp from the 5' end of Read 2 of paired-end sequencing results only. Since the first couple of bases in Read 2 of BS-Seq experiments show a severe bias towards non-methylation as a result of end-repairing sonicated fragments with unmethylated cytosines (see M-bias plot), it is recommended that the first couple of bp of Read 2 are removed before starting downstream analysis. Please see the section on M-bias plots in the Bismark User Guide for more details.

ignore_3prime_r2.description: Ignore methylation in last n bases of 3' end of R2
ignore_3prime_r2.help_text: Ignore the last <int> bp from the 3' end of Read 1 (or single-end alignment files) when processing the methylation call string. This can remove unwanted biases from the end of reads.

known_splices.description: Supply a .gtf file containing known splice sites (bismark_hisat only).
known_splices.help_text:
Specify to run Bismark with the `--known-splicesite-infile` flag to run splice-aware alignment using HISAT2. A `.gtf` file has to be provided from which a list of known splicesites is created by the pipeline

> NB: This only works when using the `bismark_hisat` aligner with `--align`

local_alignment.description: Allow soft-clipping of reads (potentially useful for single-cell experiments).
local_alignment.help_text: Specify to run Bismark with the `--local` flag to allow soft-clipping of reads. This should only be used with care in certain single-cell applications or PBAT libraries, which may produce chimeric read pairs. (See [Wu et al.](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btz125)).

minins.description: The minimum insert size for valid paired-end alignments.
minins.help_text:
For example, if `--minins 60` is specified and a paired-end alignment consists of two 20-bp alignments in the appropriate orientation with a 20-bp gap between them, that alignment is considered valid (as long as `--maxins` is also satisfied). A 19-bp gap would not be valid in that case.

Default: no flag (Bismark default: `0`).

maxins.description: The maximum insert size for valid paired-end alignments.
maxins.help_text:
For example, if `--maxins 100` is specified and a paired-end alignment consists of two 20-bp alignments in the proper orientation with a 60-bp gap between them, that alignment is considered valid (as long as `--minins` is also satisfied). A 61-bp gap would not be valid in that case.

Default: not specified. Bismark default: `500`.

nomeseq.description: Sample is NOMe-seq or NMT-seq. Runs coverage2cytosine.
nomeseq.help_text:
Sets `--CX` during methylation extraction and `--nome` during the `coverage2cytosine` step.

Will also force the coverage2cytosine step to run.

comprehensive.description: Merges methylation calls for every strand into a single, context dependent file.
comprehensive.help_text: By default `bismark_methylation_extractor` will produce a strand-specific output named as OT, OB, CTOT or CTOB. This flag will merge all strands into a single, context dependent file.

all_contexts.description: Call methylation in all three CpG, CHG and CHH contexts.
all_contexts.help_text: By default MethylDackel calls methylation just in the CpG context. The `--all_contexts` parameter sets MethylDackel to run with options `--CHH` and `--CHG` to call methylation in all three contexts.

merge_context.description: Merges methylation metrics of the Cytosines in a given context.
merge_context.help_text: By default methylation results are provided at the Cytosine level. This parameter specifies MethylDackel to run with the `--mergeContext` option, which will merge the metrics of the Cytosines in contexts CpG and CHG.

min_depth.description: Specify a minimum read coverage for MethylDackel to report a methylation call.

ignore_flags.help_text: Run MethylDackel with the `--ignore_flags` option, to ignore SAM flags.

methyl_kit.description: Save files for use with methylKit
methyl_kit.help_text: Run MethylDackel with the `--methyl_kit` option, to produce files suitable for use with the methylKit R package.

trim_OT.description: Nucleotides to exclude from methylation calling on Original Top (strand) reads, following this pattern: R1 start, R1 end, R2 start, R2 end

trim_OB.description: Nucleotides to exclude from methylation calling on Original Bottom (strand) reads, following this pattern: R1 start, R1 end, R2 start, R2 end

bamqc_regions_file.description: A GFF or BED file containing the target regions which will be passed to Qualimap/Bamqc.
bamqc_regions_file.help_text: Setting this option could be useful if you want calculate coverage stats over a list of regions, i.e. for targeted methylation sequencing data.

target_regions_file.description: A BED file containing the target regions
target_regions_file.help_text: This file will be used for filtering the bedGraph file with the methylation results

collecthsmetrics.description: Run Picard CollectHsMetrics in the targeted analysis
collecthsmetrics.help_text: Instructs the pipeline to run `picard CollectHsMetrics` with the target regions BED on the BAM files to estimate several enrichment metrics

skip_deduplication.help_text:
Deduplication removes PCR duplicate reads after alignment. Specifying this option will skip this step, leaving duplicate reads in your data.

Note that this is turned on automatically if `--rrbs` is specified.

run_targeted_sequencing.description: Run advanced analysis for targeted methylation kits with enrichment of specific regions

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

hook_url.description: Incoming hook URL for messaging service
hook_url.help_text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
